identity.title: Prescriptive Scaling Reveals the Evolution of Language Model Capabilities

problem.claim: Determine attainable downstream accuracy from a pre-training compute budget under contemporary post-training, and assess whether this mapping remains stable as the field evolves.

contributions.claim: Estimates capability boundaries with smoothed quantile regression using a monotone, saturating sigmoid parameterization.
Analyzes temporal stability, task-dependent saturation, and contamination-related shifts, including math reasoning.
Releases the Proteus-2k evaluation dataset and introduces an algorithm that recovers near-full-data frontiers using roughly 20% of the evaluation budget.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they introduce a practical methodology for translating compute budgets into performance expectations and monitoring moving capability boundaries, alongside the Proteus-2k dataset.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report fitting on earlier model generations and evaluating on later releases to validate temporal reliability.
The authors report that estimated boundaries are mostly stable across tasks, except for a consistently advancing math-reasoning boundary.
The authors report using 5k observational and 2k newly sampled performance data, and recovering near-full-data frontiers with roughly 20% of evaluation budget.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames prescriptive scaling as the attainable downstream accuracy and temporal stability associated with a pre-training compute budget.
Uses large-scale observational evaluations and quantile regression to estimate high-score capability boundaries as a function of log pre-training FLOPs.
Tests earlier-to-later generalization, reports mostly stable boundaries with advancing math reasoning, and examines saturation and contamination-related shifts.
Introduces Proteus-2k and an evaluation-budget-efficient frontier-recovery algorithm.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates attainable performance under current practice from whether the compute-to-performance mapping remains stable, then tests temporal reliability explicitly.

lessons.interpretation: This separation helps distinguish a scaling estimate from an assumption that its boundary will persist.
lessons.application: When presenting a predictive scaling relationship, state its deployment conditions and add an out-of-time evaluation to test boundary drift.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when later releases or comparable time-indexed data are unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark identities, model-generation counts, regression details, uncertainty estimates, or the metric used for temporal reliability.
The contamination-related analysis and the precise meaning of near-full-data frontier recovery are not reported in detail.

editorial_revisions.after: Releases the Proteus-2k evaluation dataset and introduces an algorithm that recovers near-full-data frontiers using roughly 20% of the evaluation budget.
